what_its_for: Zanubrutinib is a cancer medicine used to treat certain types of blood cancers, including mantle cell lymphoma, chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL), small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL), Waldenström's macroglobulinemia, follicular lymphoma, and marginal zone lymphoma. It works by blocking a protein called BTK (Bruton's tyrosine kinase) that cancer cells need to grow and survive.
how_to_take: Swallow the capsules whole with a glass of water. You can take zanubrutinib with or without food — it does not matter. Do not open, crush, or chew the capsules. Try to take it at the same time(s) every day to keep a steady level of medicine in your body.
dosing: The usual dose is either 160 mg (two 80 mg capsules) taken TWICE daily, OR 320 mg (four 80 mg capsules) taken ONCE daily, depending on what your doctor prescribes. Your doctor may adjust your dose based on your condition, other medicines you take, or any side effects you experience. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but ONLY if it is within 8 hours of your scheduled time. If more than 8 hours have passed, skip the missed dose completely and take your next dose at the regular scheduled time. Never double up or take two doses at once to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store zanubrutinib at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it in the original container, away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Keep it out of the reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about the best way to safely dispose of any leftover medication.
what_to_avoid: Avoid grapefruit, grapefruit juice, Seville oranges, and starfruit, as they can increase the amount of zanubrutinib in your blood and raise the risk of side effects. Avoid St. John's Wort supplements, as they can make the medicine less effective. Tell your doctor and pharmacist about ALL medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take, because many common drugs (including certain antifungals, antibiotics, seizure medicines, and blood thinners) can interact with zanubrutinib. Avoid activities with a high risk of bleeding or injury, since this medicine can increase your bleeding risk. Do not receive live vaccines while taking this medicine without first checking with your doctor.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: unusual bleeding or bruising (such as blood in urine or stool, coughing up blood, or prolonged bleeding from a cut); signs of serious infection such as fever over 100.4°F (38°C), chills, or feeling very unwell; chest pain, shortness of breath, or a fast or irregular heartbeat (signs of heart rhythm problems); severe headache, weakness, numbness, or vision changes (possible signs of stroke or bleeding in the brain); swollen lymph nodes or rapidly growing lumps; painful skin rash or blisters; or signs of a serious allergic reaction such as swelling of the face, lips, or throat, difficulty breathing, or hives. Also call your doctor if you are planning any surgery, dental procedure, or if you become pregnant.
when_it_works: Zanubrutinib begins working in your body right away after you take it, but you may not feel or notice the effects immediately. Your doctor will check blood tests and imaging studies over weeks to months to see how well the medicine is working. Some patients see improvements within a few weeks, while for others it may take several months. It is very important to keep taking this medicine every day, even if you feel well, unless your doctor tells you to stop.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Zanubrutinib can harm an unborn baby. Women who can become pregnant should use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 1 week after the last dose. Men with female partners who could become pregnant should also use birth control during treatment and for 1 week after stopping. Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine and for 2 weeks after the last dose. Older adults (age 65+): This medicine can be used in older adults, but they may be more sensitive to side effects such as infections and bleeding — your doctor will monitor you closely. Kidney or liver problems: Your doctor may adjust your dose if you have moderate to severe liver problems. Tell your doctor about any kidney or liver issues before starting this medicine.
